critical_issues.msg: Plan acceptance criterion (line 39) requires 'rendered markdown via react-markdown' for ticket descriptions, but the description block renders plain text with whitespace-pre-wrap — no actual markdown processing occurs.
critical_issues.suggestion:
Import react-markdown and replace

{ticket.description}

with {ticket.description}.

critical_issues.msg: Customer sidebar shows '// {ticket.customer_id}' (raw ID) with no link or name, creating a poor UX with no way to navigate to the customer.
critical_issues.suggestion: Use useCustomers() to look up the customer name by ID and render a customer link, or at minimum render the ID as clickable text that links to /customers/{id}.

critical_issues.msg: useUsers is called with two arguments (1, 100) but only accepts one parameter (page) per queries.ts line 249, making page_size a no-op and returning at most 20 users.
critical_issues.suggestion: Change useUsers(1, 100) to useUsers(1) and update the useUsers query in queries.ts to accept an optional page_size parameter, e.g.: useUsers(page = 1, page_size = 100).

critical_issues.msg: Identical signature mismatch to page.tsx line 194: useUsers(1, 100) passes two args but useUsers only accepts page, so only the first 20 agents are loaded and bulk-assign may miss most agents.
critical_issues.suggestion: Update the useUsers query in queries.ts to accept an optional second parameter (page_size), e.g.: export function useUsers(page = 1, page_size = 20), then update both call sites to pass the desired page size.

critical_issues.msg: update_ticket UPDATE WHERE clause is missing tenant_id — all four update operations (this method, change_status, add_reply) will update tickets across any tenant, violating multi-tenancy.
critical_issues.suggestion: Add .where(TicketModel.tenant_id == tenant_id) to every update() call: update(TicketModel).where(and_(TicketModel.id == ticket_id, TicketModel.tenant_id == tenant_id)).values(...)

critical_issues.msg: change_status UPDATE WHERE omits tenant_id — same multi-tenancy violation as update_ticket.
critical_issues.suggestion: Add tenant_id to the where clause: .where(and_(TicketModel.id == ticket_id, TicketModel.tenant_id == tenant_id))

critical_issues.msg: add_reply UPDATE for first_response_at omits tenant_id — updates across all tenants.
critical_issues.suggestion: Add tenant_id to the where clause: .where(and_(TicketModel.id == ticket_id, TicketModel.tenant_id == tenant_id))

critical_issues.msg: TicketUpdate.assigned_to is defined with ge=0 (allows 0), but test_test_assign_ticket.py asserts 0 is rejected with status 422. The test expectation contradicts the schema definition — at runtime, Pydantic will accept 0 and the test will fail.
critical_issues.suggestion: Change TicketUpdate.assigned_to to Field(ge=1) to match the test's expectation that 0 is invalid, or update the test assertion if 0 should be allowed.

suggestions.msg: Acceptance criterion requires 'rendered markdown via react-markdown' for ticket descriptions, but no such dependency is mentioned in the plan.
suggestions.suggestion: Add 'react-markdown' to the Affected Files list and ensure it is listed in frontend/package.json dependencies.

suggestions.msg: reply.id is cast to number (as number) but if the API returns id as a string (e.g. UUID), this produces NaN as a React key, causing all replies to share the same key.
suggestions.suggestion: Use String(reply.id) as the key instead of as number, or guard with typeof reply.id === 'number'.

suggestions.msg: ticket.channel is cast to string but may be null; the capitalizing call (ticket.channel as string) is therefore unreliable — null becomes 'null'.
suggestions.suggestion: Use (ticket.channel ?? '—') and apply .charAt(0).toUpperCase() + .slice(1) only when non-null, or use an explicit STATUS_LABELS map.

suggestions.msg: useAddReply onSuccess invalidates ticket replies cache but does not invalidate the activity log, so the new reply will not appear in the activity log section until a page refresh.
suggestions.suggestion: In queries.ts useAddReply onSuccess, add: qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: qk.ticketActivity(vars.ticketId) }).

suggestions.msg: TicketFormDialog edit mode does not expose sla_level or response_deadline fields, so an agent cannot adjust SLA settings from the edit dialog.
suggestions.suggestion: Add sla_level Select to the TicketFormDialog when isEditing is true, mapped to the ticket's sla_level field.

suggestions.msg: eslint-disable-next-line comment suppresses the exhaustive-deps rule; the dependency array intentionally omits breachedTicketIds, but this pattern is fragile and masks a genuine stale-closure risk.
suggestions.suggestion: Refactor the toast logic so breachedTicketIds is a proper dependency, or move the logic into a useCallback/useEffect combo that avoids the suppression.

suggestions.msg: useEffect dependency array lists isLoading and breachedTicketIds, but the effect reads page, sortKey, sortDir, debouncedKeyword, priorityFilter, channelFilter, assigneeFilter which are not listed, creating a stale-closure risk for future sort/filter operations.
suggestions.suggestion: Wrap the sorted list computation in useMemo and list all dependencies explicitly, removing the eslint-disable suppression.

suggestions.msg: SLA breach toast fires on every page switch (setPage resets page state) even after toastsShownRef is true, because breachedTicketIds is a new Set object on each render whose size is always > 0 for already-breached tickets.
suggestions.suggestion: Move breachedTicketIds construction into useMemo keyed on slaBreachesData to avoid creating a new Set reference on every render.

suggestions.msg: bulkUpdate.mutateAsync is called without invalidating ticket replies or activity caches; after a bulk status change, stale ticket list data persists in React Query cache.
suggestions.suggestion: In queries.ts useBulkUpdateTickets onSuccess, broaden the invalidation to include all ticket-related keys: qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['tickets'] }).

suggestions.msg: BulkActionsBar renders nothing when selectedIds is empty but still mounts and imports useUsers/useBulkUpdateTickets even when zero tickets are selected, wasting query resources.
suggestions.suggestion: Consider splitting: pass selectedIds.size as a prop and guard the query hooks inside the component as currently done, since the component returns null early this is acceptable but could be more explicit.

suggestions.msg: ruff linting is configured but ruff formatter configuration is absent — format check will not run in CI.
suggestions.suggestion: Add [tool.ruff.format] section with e.g. quote-style = "double", or rely on ruff check alone but document the gap.

suggestions.msg: bulk_update_tickets performs N+1 validation queries (one per ticket_id) before any updates, making the endpoint O(N) extra round-trips.
suggestions.suggestion: Use a single SELECT COUNT or SELECT id WHERE id IN (...) AND tenant_id = ... to pre-validate all ticket IDs in one query, then proceed with bulk updates.

suggestions.msg: SLAService instantiated with a second TicketService(session) — wasteful, creates two service instances for the same session.
suggestions.suggestion: Reuse the already-instantiated ticket_svc: pass ticket_svc (defined on line 318) to SLAService instead of constructing a new TicketService(session).

suggestions.msg: _next_agent uses global ticket count modulo pool size as a round-robin strategy — this is not safe under concurrent writes (race condition) and ignores agent workload.
suggestions.suggestion: Use a proper agent-load balancing query (e.g. select agent with fewest open tickets) or accept this as a known limitation documented in a comment.

suggestions.msg: get_ticket_activity uses LIKE pattern-match on ticket ID string rather than a proper foreign-key relationship, making it fragile and O(N) on activity table size with no index utilization.
suggestions.suggestion: Add opportunity_id=None AND content type tag as a signal, or use a dedicated ticket_activity table with a ticket_id FK column.

suggestions.msg: get_customer_tickets returns all matching tickets with no pagination — large customers could return unbounded result sets.
suggestions.suggestion: Add page/page_size parameters to match the list_tickets API contract.

suggestions.msg: test_auto_assign_assigns_agents_round_robin asserts that two tickets get different (or same) agents but does not verify that agent assignment is tenant-scoped — concurrent test runs across tenants will interfere with the count-based round-robin.
suggestions.suggestion: Add assertion that ticket1.assigned_to != ticket2.assigned_to OR document that round-robin is per-tenant and add a tenant-isolation test.

suggestions.msg: test_get_ticket_activity_returns_list only asserts that the result is a list — it does not verify that activity records are scoped to the correct ticket_id.
suggestions.suggestion: Seed an activity record for the ticket and assert its content/ID is returned; assert that an unrelated ticket's activity is not included.

suggestions.msg: MockTicketModel.check_sla_breach uses datetime.now() at call-time for the breach check, but the actual Ticket model uses datetime.now(UTC) — test uses local timezone while the real code uses UTC (models/ticket.py:59).
suggestions.suggestion: Use datetime.now(UTC) in MockTicketModel.check_sla_breach to match the production implementation.

suggestions.msg: MockRow in test_ticket_service.py duplicates MockRow from tests/unit/conftest.py — CLAUDE.md rule 110: avoid copy-paste duplication across modules.
suggestions.suggestion: Import MockRow and MockResult from tests.unit.conftest instead of defining local copies in test_ticket_service.py.

suggestions.msg: MockResult.scalars() returns a MagicMock that loses type safety — result.scalars().all() returns a plain MagicMock, not a list of actual objects. This can silently hide bugs if scalars() is called with different arguments in production.
suggestions.suggestion: Use the real MockResult from tests.unit.conftest (which properly implements scalars() as a MagicMock returning the actual rows list), or make the local MockResult.scalars() return self._rows for consistency.

suggestions.msg: mock_session fixture does not set __aenter__ and __aexit__, so async context manager usage (e.g. 'async with session:') will fail silently in tests that try it, unlike real AsyncSession.
suggestions.suggestion: Add AsyncMock side effects for __aenter__ and __aexit__ to mock_session, or use make_mock_session from conftest which properly implements the async context manager protocol.

suggestions.msg: Test verifies SQL ordering via str() of SQL text, which is a fragile proxy — string-based assertion on SQL is not a reliable contract (conftest.py's handler lowercases and normalizes SQL text, which may not match what the service actually sends).
suggestions.suggestion: Assert on the actual result objects rather than SQL string inspection, or mock session.execute at a higher level to verify the query parameters passed rather than the SQL text.

suggestions.msg: tickets_router uses 'async with get_db_session()' style in docstrings, but actual routes inject session via Depends(get_db) — the docstring example is misleading and does not match the implementation.
suggestions.suggestion: Update the docstring example in db/connection.py to use 'session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)' consistent with how routes actually receive the session.

suggestions.msg: client_with_service overrides get_db with lambda: MagicMock() — the session has no async context manager (__aenter__/__aexit__) support, so any route that uses 'async with session:' would fail, though this appears not to occur in current routes.
suggestions.suggestion: Ensure the mock session returned by the override has proper __aenter__/__aexit__ AsyncMocks, or document why routes never use async with pattern.

suggestions.msg: page_size=101 test asserts 422 but doesn't verify the constraint actually comes from the router Query(ge=1, le=100) rather than from Pydantic — if the constraint moved to Pydantic, this test would still pass but for the wrong reason.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a comment noting that the 422 for page_size=101 derives from the router's Query(le=100) constraint, not a Pydantic model.

suggestions.msg: Test SLAStatusEndpoint mocks calculate_remaining_time returning a MagicMock with nested total_seconds() returning another MagicMock — this is indirect and fragile. The test verifies response structure but not correctness of the actual SLA calculation logic.
suggestions.suggestion: Consider testing SLAService.calculate_remaining_time directly rather than through a router-level mock that buries the assertion in nested MagicMock stubs.

suggestions.msg: monkeypatch.setattr is used on TicketService, SLAService, UserService classes before app is created — if any of those imports fail, the fixture will not clean up properly and subsequent tests may get partial mocks.
suggestions.suggestion: Add error handling or a teardown step to ensure the fixture is resilient to import-time failures in the target module.

issues.suggestion: Use a single SELECT COUNT or SELECT id WHERE id IN (...) AND tenant_id = ... to pre-validate all ticket IDs in one query, then proceed with bulk updates.

issues.message: SLAService instantiated with a second TicketService(session) — wasteful, creates two service instances for the same session.
issues.suggestion: Reuse the already-instantiated ticket_svc: pass ticket_svc (defined on line 318) to SLAService instead of constructing a new TicketService(session).

parsed.summary: Router correctly follows the pattern (service returns ORM, router serializes to dict); request schemas use Pydantic Field validation throughout.

issues.message: update_ticket UPDATE WHERE clause is missing tenant_id — all four update operations (this method, change_status, add_reply) will update tickets across any tenant, violating multi-tenancy.
issues.suggestion: Add .where(TicketModel.tenant_id == tenant_id) to every update() call: update(TicketModel).where(and_(TicketModel.id == ticket_id, TicketModel.tenant_id == tenant_id)).values(...)

issues.message: change_status UPDATE WHERE omits tenant_id — same multi-tenancy violation as update_ticket.
issues.suggestion: Add tenant_id to the where clause: .where(and_(TicketModel.id == ticket_id, TicketModel.tenant_id == tenant_id))

issues.message: add_reply UPDATE for first_response_at omits tenant_id — updates across all tenants.
issues.suggestion: Add tenant_id to the where clause: .where(and_(TicketModel.id == ticket_id, TicketModel.tenant_id == tenant_id))

issues.message: _next_agent uses global ticket count modulo pool size as a round-robin strategy — this is not safe under concurrent writes (race condition) and ignores agent workload.
issues.suggestion: Use a proper agent-load balancing query (e.g. select agent with fewest open tickets) or accept this as a known limitation documented in a comment.

issues.message: get_ticket_activity uses LIKE pattern-match on ticket ID string rather than a proper foreign-key relationship, making it fragile and O(N) on activity table size with no index utilization.
issues.suggestion: Add opportunity_id=None AND content type tag as a signal, or use a dedicated ticket_activity table with a ticket_id FK column.

issues.message: get_customer_tickets returns all matching tickets with no pagination — large customers could return unbounded result sets.
issues.suggestion: Add page/page_size parameters to match the list_tickets API contract.

parsed.summary: ticket_service.py has correct service-layer patterns (session injection, raise-on-error, no commit) but all three UPDATE statements omit tenant_id from the WHERE clause — a critical multi-tenancy data leak.

issues.message: test_auto_assign_assigns_agents_round_robin asserts that two tickets get different (or same) agents but does not verify that agent assignment is tenant-scoped — concurrent test runs across tenants will interfere with the count-based round-robin.
issues.suggestion: Add assertion that ticket1.assigned_to != ticket2.assigned_to OR document that round-robin is per-tenant and add a tenant-isolation test.

issues.message: test_get_ticket_activity_returns_list only asserts that the result is a list — it does not verify that activity records are scoped to the correct ticket_id.
issues.suggestion: Seed an activity record for the ticket and assert its content/ID is returned; assert that an unrelated ticket's activity is not included.

parsed.summary: Integration tests correctly use real DB fixtures (db_schema, tenant_id, async_session) and no DB mocking; test coverage is solid for core flows but activity and auto-assign tests are thin.

issues.message: MockTicketModel.check_sla_breach uses datetime.now() at call-time for the breach check, but the actual Ticket model uses datetime.now(UTC) — test uses local timezone while the real code uses UTC (models/ticket.py:59).
issues.suggestion: Use datetime.now(UTC) in MockTicketModel.check_sla_breach to match the production implementation.

issues.message: MockRow in test_ticket_service.py duplicates MockRow from tests/unit/conftest.py — CLAUDE.md rule 110: avoid copy-paste duplication across modules.
issues.suggestion: Import MockRow and MockResult from tests.unit.conftest instead of defining local copies in test_ticket_service.py.

issues.message: MockResult.scalars() returns a MagicMock that loses type safety — result.scalars().all() returns a plain MagicMock, not a list of actual objects. This can silently hide bugs if scalars() is called with different arguments in production.
issues.suggestion: Use the real MockResult from tests.unit.conftest (which properly implements scalars() as a MagicMock returning the actual rows list), or make the local MockResult.scalars() return self._rows for consistency.

issues.message: mock_session fixture does not set __aenter__ and __aexit__, so async context manager usage (e.g. 'async with session:') will fail silently in tests that try it, unlike real AsyncSession.
issues.suggestion: Add AsyncMock side effects for __aenter__ and __aexit__ to mock_session, or use make_mock_session from conftest which properly implements the async context manager protocol.

issues.message: Test verifies SQL ordering via str() of SQL text, which is a fragile proxy — string-based assertion on SQL is not a reliable contract (conftest.py's handler lowercases and normalizes SQL text, which may not match what the service actually sends).
issues.suggestion: Assert on the actual result objects rather than SQL string inspection, or mock session.execute at a higher level to verify the query parameters passed rather than the SQL text.

parsed.summary: Tests correctly validate behavior but reimplement mock primitives already available in conftest.py, and one test checks SQL string representation which is fragile.

issues.message: TicketUpdate.assigned_to is defined with ge=0 (allows 0), but test_test_assign_ticket.py asserts 0 is rejected with status 422. The test expectation contradicts the schema definition — at runtime, Pydantic will accept 0 and the test will fail.
issues.suggestion: Change TicketUpdate.assigned_to to Field(ge=1) to match the test's expectation that 0 is invalid, or update the test assertion if 0 should be allowed.

issues.message: tickets_router uses 'async with get_db_session()' style in docstrings, but actual routes inject session via Depends(get_db) — the docstring example is misleading and does not match the implementation.
issues.suggestion: Update the docstring example in db/connection.py to use 'session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)' consistent with how routes actually receive the session.

issues.message: client_with_service overrides get_db with lambda: MagicMock() — the session has no async context manager (__aenter__/__aexit__) support, so any route that uses 'async with session:' would fail, though this appears not to occur in current routes.
issues.suggestion: Ensure the mock session returned by the override has proper __aenter__/__aexit__ AsyncMocks, or document why routes never use async with pattern.

issues.message: page_size=101 test asserts 422 but doesn't verify the constraint actually comes from the router Query(ge=1, le=100) rather than from Pydantic — if the constraint moved to Pydantic, this test would still pass but for the wrong reason.
issues.suggestion: Add a comment noting that the 422 for page_size=101 derives from the router's Query(le=100) constraint, not a Pydantic model.

issues.message: Test SLAStatusEndpoint mocks calculate_remaining_time returning a MagicMock with nested total_seconds() returning another MagicMock — this is indirect and fragile. The test verifies response structure but not correctness of the actual SLA calculation logic.
issues.suggestion: Consider testing SLAService.calculate_remaining_time directly rather than through a router-level mock that buries the assertion in nested MagicMock stubs.

issues.message: monkeypatch.setattr is used on TicketService, SLAService, UserService classes before app is created — if any of those imports fail, the fixture will not clean up properly and subsequent tests may get partial mocks.
issues.suggestion: Add error handling or a teardown step to ensure the fixture is resilient to import-time failures in the target module.

parsed.summary: Tests are comprehensive and well-structured; one critical mismatch exists between the TicketUpdate schema (ge=0 allows 0) and the test asserting 0 is rejected (expected 422), which will cause the test to fail at runtime.
